_about: The voice-in spike's phrase sheet (2026-10-23, inbox drain; design: Rio 10-21/10-22, Andrew's play-button amendment). Rows of data. TARGET rows sit on a SOUND fault line, chosen so the planted error turns the word into another word where Tamil allows it; Andrew records a good take and a bad take shaped down from the reference. TANGLISH rows are how he will actually talk to Anna, one take. FREE rows have no target: the reference plays Anna's question and he answers however he likes, one take, then types what he meant. `ask` is the lesson moment the IN-CONTEXT condition is told about.

phrases.fault: zha as an English l: malai (mountain) varudhu
phrases.ask: Look outside and tell me what the weather is doing.
Ask your aunt for a banana.
Tell me the kids are asleep.

phrases.fault: the hard trilled Ra as a soft English r: nirudhunga
phrases.ask: Tell the auto driver to stop here.

phrases.fault: Ra as a soft r, short tten: marandhuten
phrases.ask: Tell me you forgot.

phrases.fault: kaRi with a soft r is kari (charcoal)
phrases.ask: Praise the curry.

phrases.fault: the retroflex NN as a flat English n
phrases.ask: Ask for some water.

phrases.fault: the NR cluster flattened to English nr: panreenga
phrases.ask: Ask your uncle what he's up to.

phrases.fault: the retroflex tt as dental: paaththu (look)
phrases.ask: Ask your niece to sing.

phrases.fault: every long aa short: vanga, ukkarunga
phrases.ask: Welcome a guest in and seat them.
Suggest watching a film tonight.
Tell me your leg hurts after the walk.

phrases.fault: the double ll single, the aa short: nalarukku
phrases.ask: Tell her the food is really good.

phrases.fault: the long -om ending swallowed into an English schwa: ponum
phrases.ask: Tell me you all went yesterday.

phrases.fault: the question -aa clipped and the dh hardened: podhum, with an English d
phrases.ask: Ask if that's enough rice.

phrases.fault: the reduced Kongu form spelled out in full, book style: saappitteergalaa
phrases.ask: Ask your mother-in-law if she has eaten.

phrases.say: Office-ல work ரொம்ப heavy, அதான் late-ஆ வரேன்.
phrases.roman: Office-la work romba heavy, adhaan late-aa varen.
phrases.en: work at the office is really heavy, that's why I'm coming late
phrases.ask: Why are you late tonight?

phrases.say: Weekend-ல family-ஓட beach-க்கு போனோம், super-ஆ இருந்துச்சு.
phrases.roman: Weekend-la family-oda beach-ku ponom, super-aa irundhuchu.
phrases.en: we went to the beach with the family at the weekend, it was great
phrases.ask: What did you do at the weekend?

phrases.say: Sorry, எனக்கு புரியல, கொஞ்சம் slow-ஆ சொல்லுங்க.

phrases.en: sorry, I didn't understand, say it a bit slower
phrases.ask: (Anna just said something fast that he missed.)
What did you do today?
